stories.title: Stanford's Memorilla packs a whole document store into 16 tokens
stories.plain: Stanford researchers open-sourced Memorilla, a small add-on that lets an unchanged language model answer questions about a large pile of documents while only seeing 16 special 'memory' tokens. On several benchmarks it beats simply pasting all the documents into the prompt, and it answers far faster.
stories.eng: Documents are embedded once by a frozen Qwen3-Embedding-4B encoder into a persistent store; only new or changed documents are re-encoded. Per query, a trainable 194M-parameter Perceiver-style module with 16 slots conditions on the query, cross-attends over every stored embedding, and projects the result into the frozen Qwen3-8B's input-embedding space as 16 soft tokens prepended to the question. No LLM weights change; training ran in three stages (paraphrase reconstruction, QA and summarisation, then a benchmark mixture).
specs: 0.74 s vs 19.9 s full context (1 H100)
Code Apache 2.0, checkpoints on Hugging Face
stories.point: The point: 'memory' for a model does not have to mean a longer prompt or a retrieval pipeline; a small learned compressor in front of a frozen model can do better on less.
stories.means: Today there are two main ways to give a model your documents: paste them all into the context window (slow and expensive, and quality drops as the prompt grows) or retrieve a few chunks with RAG (cheap, but you miss whatever the retriever skipped). Memorilla takes a third path: it reads every stored document as a vector and squeezes what is relevant to this specific question into 16 vectors the model reads as if they were words. Across eight benchmarks it used on average 394x fewer document tokens than full context and 113x fewer than a 50-chunk RAG setup, while scoring higher than xRAG, LLMLingua-2 and Mem0. It is not better everywhere: on PubMedQA it scored 59% against 69% for LLMLingua-2, and the authors say fine-grained facts can get lost.
stories.industry: Long context is one of the biggest cost drivers in agent workloads, where the same files and history are re-read on every turn. Methods that keep the base model frozen are attractive because they can sit in front of any deployed model without retraining it. The catch for now is that it was only tested with a Qwen encoder and Qwen decoder.
stories.you: If you run RAG or long-context prompts over a fixed corpus, this is worth a weekend test: the repo takes a parquet file of documents and questions with no code changes and evaluation takes about 15 minutes per checkpoint. Watch accuracy on exact-detail questions such as IDs, numbers and quotes, where compression is weakest.
terms: Soft token
A learned vector fed to the model in place of a word embedding; it carries information but is not readable text.
Frozen model
A model whose weights are not changed; only a small attached module is trained.
Perceiver-style
An architecture where a few learned slots use cross-attention to summarise a much larger input.
stories.why: On the interactive TextWorld task the memory module raised average success from 18.6% to 24.2%, a hint it can carry agent state as well as documents.
stories.source: MarkTechPost · 14 Nov; arXiv 2610.21375; snap-stanford/memorilla on GitHub

stories.title: Robot exam for coding agents: best score 34% on realistic tests
stories.plain: A large group of US universities released Embodied First Exam, a benchmark where AI coding agents must make simulated robots complete physical tasks. With full access to the simulator the best agent solves most tests, but with only normal sensor readings the top score is 34%.
stories.eng: Agents (a model inside a harness such as Codex or Claude Code) get a robot API and choose how to act: direct commands, writing a control program, or training a policy. Three protocols: Privileged (full state, unlimited resets), Standard (sensor observations only, simulation pauses between calls) and Realtime (simulation keeps running). Grading is done by a verifier outside the agent's container.
specs: 63% of tests unsolved by every agent
Same model: 34% in Codex, 22% in Claude Code
stories.point: The point: coding agents can plan robot work, but they still fall apart when they cannot peek at the true state of the world or undo mistakes.
stories.means: Most robot benchmarks test a specialised control model. This one asks whether general coding agents, the same ones people use to write software, can operate robots end to end. The gap between 77% and 30% shows what usually makes it easy: with exact object positions and free resets, the agent can just try again. The authors found resets matter more than perfect state: for GPT-6 Astra, adding exact state lifted success from 28% to 45%, resets alone to 53%, and both to 68%. Failures cluster at precise steps such as tight fits and moving contact. All results are in simulation, with one attempt per test.
stories.industry: Labs are betting that general frontier models will run robots rather than separate robot brains; OpenAI said as much this week. This benchmark gives a sober number for where that bet stands. The 12-point swing from changing only the harness also shows that agent scaffolding is as important as the model.
stories.you: If you build agents that act on anything you cannot cheaply roll back (infrastructure, payments, devices), the lesson carries over: success depends heavily on having a reset or sandbox. And when you compare models, hold the harness constant or your numbers mean little.
terms: Harness
The software around a model that gives it tools, files and a loop to act in, such as Codex or Claude Code.
Privileged state
Exact simulator data (object positions, physics) that a real robot would never get.
Policy
A trained controller that maps observations to robot actions.
stories.why: Authors come from Northwestern, CMU, UC Berkeley, Stanford, the University of Washington and other US universities; the paper was posted on 9 Nov and picked up widely this weekend.

stories.title: OpenAI folds its robotics team into core research
stories.plain: OpenAI disbanded its standalone robotics team and moved the researchers into its main research group, with hardware staff going to its applied product group. The company says its general models, such as GPT-6 Astra, can now control robots directly, and it still plans to show its own humanoid in 2027.
stories.eng: Research staff now report to chief research officer Mark Chen; applied robotics and hardware staff join the Applied org under president Greg Brockman. The main public evidence is an Nvidia simulation study in which GPT-6 Astra, used as a robot controller on a pick-and-place benchmark, beat the best dedicated robot model, though at high cost and latency per step.
specs: GPT-6 Astra 74.8% vs 51% best robot model
stories.point: The point: OpenAI is betting robotics is a capability of its general models, not a separate product line, and is reorganising around that bet.
stories.means: Robot companies have usually trained dedicated 'vision-language-action' models on robot demonstration data, which is scarce and expensive to collect. OpenAI's claim is that its frontier model has absorbed enough about the physical world to plan and control robot actions without that specialised training. The 74.8% result is real but comes from simulation, and at 18.56 seconds per call and about $36 per attempt it is far too slow and costly for a factory line. This is also OpenAI's third robotics reset: it wound down a team in 2020, rebuilt one in 2024, and ended its Figure partnership in February 2025.
stories.industry: If general models really generalise to robots, the advantage moves to whoever has the biggest model and compute, and specialised robot-model startups face pressure. If not, it leaves room for companies collecting real robot data. Today's Embodied First Exam results show general agents still struggle on realistic robot tasks.
stories.you: Expect robotics to show up as tool-use and agent features in general model APIs rather than as separate robot models from OpenAI. For anything latency-sensitive, a big model planning and a small local controller executing is still the practical design.
terms: VLA model
Vision-language-action model: a model trained to turn camera input and instructions into robot motor commands.
Embodied AI
AI that perceives and acts in the physical world through a body such as a robot.
stories.why: OpenAI had booked a booth at the CoRL robotics conference in Austin, which was reported empty.

stories.title: FBI warns open-source AI agent tool ARTEX is automating breaches
stories.plain: The FBI issued an alert that criminals are using ARTEX, an open-source AI agent framework built for penetration testing, to run real cyberattacks. Some intrusions went from first scan to administrator access in under three hours.
stories.eng: ARTEX is written in Go and turns natural-language objectives into commands executed by specialised agents through multi-agent orchestration. It ships no model of its own and calls external LLMs; the FBI says attacker deployments mostly use Chinese models, especially DeepSeek Flash, citing cost and weaker guardrails. The original GitHub repo was removed on 8 Oct, but forks, archives and a 'PRO' version keep it available.
stories.point: The point: autonomous hacking agents are no longer a lab demo; an off-the-shelf one is in active criminal use and the FBI is publishing hunt guidance for it.
stories.means: Penetration testing tools let security teams attack their own systems to find holes. ARTEX added AI agents that chain the steps (reconnaissance, exploitation, privilege escalation, data theft) with little human input. Once released openly, attackers adopted it within weeks, starting in August. Speed is what changes: a human team might take days to move through a network, while these agents enumerated more than 110,000 Active Directory objects and hit admin access in hours. Targets span finance, government, healthcare, energy and telecoms.
stories.industry: This sharpens the debate over open release of agent tooling and over model guardrails, since the attackers chose models with the fewest restrictions. It also pushes demand for agent-aware security products, a market that has seen several large acquisitions this month. Regulators drafting rules on dual-use AI now have a concrete case.
stories.you: The FBI's practical list is short: inventory internet-facing systems, lock down Kudu/SCM and cloud admin endpoints, tighten app consent grants, watch for new Entra credentials and rate-limit sequential portal lookups. Also alert on unexpected outbound LLM API traffic from servers that have no reason to call one.
terms: FLASH alert
An FBI technical advisory sharing indicators and mitigations for an active threat.
Privilege escalation
Moving from a limited foothold to administrator-level control of a system.
Active Directory
Microsoft's directory of users, machines and permissions in a corporate network.
stories.why: Researchers found the 1,600+ exposed ARTEX control consoles in early November, before the FBI alert.

stories.title: Apple and OpenEvidence launch a 200,000-person health AI study
stories.plain: Apple launched a study app in the US where people ask a health AI questions, rate the answers and fill in monthly surveys for at least a year. The answers come from OpenEvidence, a medical AI company that grounds its replies in journals such as NEJM, JAMA and Nature.
stories.eng: Participants use the Apple Health AI Study app; answers are generated by OpenEvidence over clinical literature. People can optionally share HealthKit data (heart rate, sleep, activity, lab results). Apple says data is anonymised before going to a third-party cloud and will not be used to train models; OpenEvidence deletes queries and responses after 24 hours.
specs: 21+, iPhone 15 or later, iOS 26+, Apple Intelligence on
stories.point: The point: Apple is collecting real-world evidence on how people use and judge medical AI before putting its own health assistant in front of its users.
stories.means: Millions of people already ask chatbots about symptoms and lab results, but there is little hard data on whether they understand the answers or act on them sensibly. Most medical AI evaluations test models on exam questions, not on ordinary people's behaviour over months. This study measures that directly: what people ask, how they rate grounded answers, and, for those who share it, how this relates to their health data. Its size and length make it one of the largest consumer health-AI studies announced.
stories.industry: Big tech is moving into AI-led health: Oura agreed to buy AI primary-care startup Counsel Health for $625M this month, and Apple has been reported to be building an AI health coach. Regulators and clinicians want evidence before these tools give personal advice; a large study is a way to generate it and to shape future rules.
stories.you: If you build anything that answers health questions, note the design choices Apple made public: answers grounded in cited literature, short retention, no training on user data, and explicit consent for sensor data. They are becoming the baseline expectation.
terms: Grounding
Making a model base its answer on specific retrieved sources rather than memory alone.
HealthKit
Apple's framework that stores health and fitness data on the iPhone and shares it with apps by consent.
stories.why: Apple's Sumbul Desai called it the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend and evaluate health AI in everyday life.

stories.title: US and nine partners sign Pax Silica declaration on AI supply chains
stories.plain: The US and nine partner countries signed the San Francisco Declaration, a joint statement on protecting the chips, infrastructure and technology behind advanced AI from undue foreign access or control. It sets up working groups rather than binding rules.
stories.eng: Signed at the Pax Silica Founders Retreat in San Francisco by the US, Australia, India, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, the UAE and the UK. It commits members to a shared understanding of the sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure in what it calls 'Super Intelligence' supply chains, to coordinated enforcement against undue access, and to joint responses to economic coercion and supply disruption.
specs: Pax Silica Founders Retreat, San Francisco
stories.point: The point: AI compute is now treated as a security alliance issue, with the US building a bloc around who can access chips, data centres and the tools to make them.
stories.means: Pax Silica is a US-led coalition on AI and semiconductor supply chains that has been forming through 2026. This declaration is its first joint text. It does not create new export rules by itself; it agrees on what counts as sensitive and sets up five working groups: pro-innovation policy, AI adoption in key sectors, supply-chain cooperation across the AI stack, safe harbours and supply-chain security hubs, and AI security and resilience. Gulf states Qatar and the UAE, both big data-centre builders, are inside the tent.
stories.industry: Export controls and chip smuggling are a live problem: this week Nvidia faced reports about a smuggling case in Taiwan, and US officials clashed over enforcement ahead of a Trump trip to China. A formal bloc makes it more likely that where you build a data centre, and whose chips you buy, will depend on membership. For cloud and chip firms this is a map of future market access.
stories.you: If your company trains or deploys in several regions, expect more paperwork on where compute sits and who can reach it, especially for frontier-scale work. The working-group topics are a preview of compliance requirements that may follow.
terms: Export controls
Government rules restricting which countries or companies may receive certain technologies, such as advanced AI chips.
Economic coercion
Using trade restrictions or supply cut-offs to pressure another country.
stories.why: The State Department frames economic security as fundamental to national security in the text's opening.

stories.title: Fed survey: 87% of market contacts now flag AI as a top risk
stories.plain: The US Federal Reserve's latest Financial Stability Report found that 87% of the market contacts it surveyed name AI as a major risk to the financial system, up from 50% in the spring. Borrowing to build AI data centres has grown fast, and much of the obligation sits off balance sheets.
stories.eng: The Fed surveyed 23 market contacts. Debt tied to advanced computing passed $680B by October, about five times 2023's total, and is roughly 31% of non-financial investment-grade corporate issuance. Seven large firms (Amazon, Alphabet, Broadcom, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, Oracle) carry over $3T in obligations not shown as ordinary debt, including more than $1T in leases not yet started.
stories.point: The point: the central bank now sees the AI build-out as a financial-system question, not just a tech story.
stories.means: Training and serving AI needs data centres that cost tens of billions each. Companies increasingly fund them with bonds, private credit and long leases rather than cash, and many lease commitments do not appear as debt in accounts. The Fed says the true exposure 'may be substantially larger' than disclosed liabilities suggest. It does not call this a bubble, and the survey is not a forecast; it measures how many professionals see AI as a risk, which has nearly tripled in a year.
stories.industry: Financing is now a constraint on AI scaling alongside chips and power. Nvidia's earnings on Tuesday, its first since its CEO resigned, will be read through this lens, as will guarantees vendors give to customers' data-centre projects. If credit tightens, the pace of new clusters slows.
stories.you: Nothing changes in your stack tomorrow, but compute pricing and availability depend on this financing holding up. If you are choosing between providers or committing to long reserved-capacity contracts, the financial health of the provider is now a reasonable thing to ask about.
terms: Off-balance-sheet
Commitments such as future leases that are not recorded as debt in a company's main accounts.
Investment-grade
Bonds rated as relatively safe by credit agencies.
stories.why: Gross leverage at the largest hedge funds is the highest since data collection began in 2013, according to summaries of the report.
stories.source: Federal Reserve report via Startup Fortune · 14 Nov

stories.title: Investors push Nvidia board to weigh Huang's return before earnings
stories.plain: Two large Nvidia shareholders asked the board to slow its CEO search and consider bringing back Jensen Huang, who resigned last week, while a public petition for his return passed 100,000 signatures. Nvidia reports quarterly results on Tuesday, its first since he left.
stories.eng: Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management sent a letter on 13 Nov asking for a 'slow, measured, and deliberate process' that weighs Huang's potential return, without demanding reinstatement. Interim CEO Colette Kress will post the written commentary for fiscal Q3. The board has not publicly responded.
stories.point: The point: the company at the centre of AI compute has a leadership vacuum just as investors start to question AI financing.
stories.means: Huang co-founded Nvidia and led it for over three decades; its CUDA software and data-centre strategy are closely tied to him. He resigned on 12 Nov after reports of extramarital relationships, and CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO. Since then the stock has fallen and its forward price-to-earnings ratio is at a one-year low. The shareholder letter matters more than the petition: it comes from funds that hold Nvidia and argues against rushing to an outside successor.
stories.industry: Nvidia's guidance is effectively a forecast for the whole AI build-out. Big customers are designing their own chips, and the Fed has just flagged AI debt as a risk. A weak quarter or unclear leadership would ripple into every company planning GPU purchases.
stories.you: Tuesday's results will move GPU pricing expectations and cloud capacity plans. For your team, the medium-term question is less who runs Nvidia than whether CUDA's lead stays strong enough to justify locking in, which is a reason to keep inference code portable where it is cheap to do so.
terms: Interim CEO
A temporary chief executive while the board searches for a permanent one.
Forward P/E
Share price divided by expected earnings over the next year; lower means investors pay less per dollar of future profit.
stories.why: The two funds held about 10.7 million Nvidia shares as of 30 June, roughly 0.04% of the company.

stories.title: Cloudflare open-sources Kitesurf, a browser engine built for agents
stories.plain: Cloudflare released the code for Kitesurf, a lightweight browser engine that lets AI agents load and read websites without running a full Chrome browser. It runs on Cloudflare's serverless platform and is free to use under an open-source licence.
stories.eng: Kitesurf is a set of Rust components compiled to WebAssembly: Blitz for HTML parsing, DOM and layout, Stylo for CSS, Linebender libraries for text and 2D graphics, and Krilla for PDFs. Page JavaScript runs in isolated Dynamic Workers, with the Boa engine as a fallback. It speaks the Chrome DevTools Protocol, so Puppeteer-style clients can connect, though not every CDP feature is supported yet.
specs: Cloudflare Workers, one Dynamic Worker per page
Rust compiled to WebAssembly, no Chromium
stories.point: The point: agents browse the web constantly, and running a full Chrome per task is the expensive part; a purpose-built engine attacks that cost directly.
stories.means: Most web agents drive headless Chrome: a full browser started in a container for each task, which uses a lot of memory and is slow to start. Kitesurf drops the container and Chromium entirely. It parses HTML, applies CSS, runs scripts and takes screenshots using compact Rust modules that start like serverless functions. Cloudflare calls it experimental: web-standard support and rendering fidelity are incomplete, so complex sites may break. It has no built-in authentication, so you need to put an auth layer in front of it.
stories.industry: Browsing is one of the most common agent tools, and infrastructure firms are competing to host it. An open engine invites others to self-host and contribute, and puts pressure on paid browser-automation services. It also fits a broader trend of rebuilding web infrastructure for machine readers, alongside protocols like WebMCP.
stories.you: If your agents only need to read pages, fill simple forms or take screenshots, Kitesurf can replace a headless Chrome fleet; you can run it locally with Wrangler before deploying. Keep Chrome as a fallback for heavy single-page apps, and secure the endpoint with Cloudflare Access or similar.
terms: Headless browser
A web browser run without a visible window, controlled by code.
Chrome DevTools Protocol
The interface tools like Puppeteer use to control a browser programmatically.
WebAssembly
A compact binary format that lets compiled code such as Rust run safely in browsers and serverless runtimes.
stories.why: Deploying to your own Cloudflare account requires a Workers Paid plan because Dynamic Workers are part of that plan.

stories.title: Atom Computing finalises $100M US award to scale quantum production
stories.plain: Neutral-atom quantum computer maker Atom Computing finalised up to $100 million in research funding from the US Department of Commerce. The money is for engineering and manufacturing so its machines can be built repeatably at larger scale.
stories.eng: Atom Computing traps individual neutral atoms with lasers and uses them as qubits, with arrays of more than 1,000 physical qubits. The award funds in-house component engineering, parallel testbeds and supply-chain integration in Boulder, Colorado, aiming to standardise production of multi-thousand-qubit arrays. The company says it has shown sub-threshold, multi-round error correction end to end.
stories.point: The point: the quantum race is moving from physics demos to factory questions, and the US government is paying to build the production line.
stories.means: Physical qubits are noisy; useful quantum computers need error correction that combines many physical qubits into one reliable 'logical' qubit. 'Sub-threshold' means errors fall as you add more qubits to the code, the key sign that scaling will help rather than hurt. Neutral-atom systems are attractive because atoms are identical and arrays can grow large, but building them repeatably needs reliable lasers, optics and vacuum systems, which is what this money targets. Atom Computing is the only neutral-atom company in Stage C of DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative.
stories.industry: Governments are treating quantum like chips: industrial policy, not just research grants. AI matters here in both directions, as machine learning is increasingly used for qubit control and error decoding, and quantum is pitched as a future accelerator for chemistry and optimisation alongside GPUs. Last week Q-CTRL raised $290M for AI-driven quantum control.
stories.you: No change for your workloads this year. If you work on scientific computing or optimisation, it is worth tracking logical-qubit counts rather than physical-qubit headlines; that is the number that decides when these machines do useful work.
terms: Neutral-atom qubit
A single uncharged atom held by laser light whose energy states store quantum information.
Logical qubit
A reliable qubit built from many error-prone physical qubits using error correction.
Sub-threshold
Operating with physical error rates low enough that adding more qubits to the code reduces overall errors.
stories.why: Atom Computing sold an on-premises logical-qubit system to the Nordic initiative QuNorth in 2025.
stories.source: Quantum Computing Report · 13 Nov; Business Wire · 13 Nov

concepts.name: Agent swarms at 1,000+
concepts.desc: What comes after orchestrating a few agents: very large teams of agents working against a strict verifier.
signals: 13 Nov
Google Antigravity /teamwork: Gemini 4 agent teams with fresh-context handoffs and falsifiers formalise the Weil conjectures and port libgav1 to faster Rust.
11 Nov
Anthropic Fellows: a single coordinator beats per-user agent teams by ~10-45 points on shared-resource tasks; MAMUBench released.
10 Nov
AlphaProof Code: Gemini-powered agents write millions of lines of Lean to verify Signal's core crypto code in about four weeks.
10 Nov
LLM proposals plus an automated evaluator beat best known quantum circuits on 7 of 8 tasks.
9 Nov
~1,000 Claude agents formalize Fermat's Last Theorem in about 30 hours.
6 Nov
Google agent teams coordinate through shared wikis and organized "conferences" to find verified quantum programs.

concepts.name: Agents that prove code correct
concepts.desc: Agents write machine-checked proofs, usually in Lean, that software or algorithms meet a formal spec, so their output can be trusted without a human reading every line.
signals: 13 Nov
Google's LEAP framework produces a ~1.8M-line machine-checked Lean formalisation of the Weil conjectures over 28,800+ subagent calls.
10 Nov
DeepMind's AlphaProof Code verifies Signal's one-to-one crypto down to machine instructions; humans review ~1% of the code.
9 Nov
~1,000 Claude agents formalize Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean in about 30 hours.
6 Nov
Google builds a Lean library where agents write quantum programs whose correctness and cost are proven.

concepts.name: Agent memory and continual learning
concepts.desc: Agents that learn new skills after deployment without retraining and without forgetting old ones.
signals: 14 Nov
Stanford open-sources Memorilla: a 194M module compresses a document store into 16 soft tokens for a frozen Qwen3-8B, beating full context on FactKG with 108x fewer tokens.
Nov
Three-part agent memory architecture lifts Opus 5.5 on CL-Bench from 0.644 to 0.833.

concepts.name: Continual world models
concepts.desc: Models that learn physics and causality from observation and keep updating after training. The bridge from text to physical tasks.
signals: Dec
NeurIPS 2026 runs a dedicated Continual World Models workshop, with papers on test-time adaptation and multi-agent world models.
11 Nov
NTT physics-constrained video world model lifts robot shelf-loading success from 73.1% to 92.3%; airport baggage trials planned with Mujin.

concepts.name: AI-discovered quantum algorithms
concepts.desc: Using LLM search to cut the gate and qubit cost of quantum algorithms, moving the date quantum becomes useful.
signals: 10 Nov
QuEra, Harvard and Anthropic publicise AI-designed circuits with up to 9,100× lower space-time cost.
6 Nov
Google preprint: agents writing Lean-verified quantum programs beat baselines by up to 290x on arithmetic and 11x on fusion-relevant simulation.
Oct
Preprint: modular inversion circuit with 17× fewer gates after a 53-hour run.

concepts.name: Instruction–data separation
concepts.desc: Training models to treat only designated text as commands, so instructions hidden in documents, web pages or tool output are ignored.
signals: 12 Nov
IBM's LLMON previews mark structure with special tokens and avoid 47% more injection attacks on OPI than the best frontier model tested.
12 Nov
Gemini 4 Hydrogen reported 2.3x more resilient to indirect prompt injection on the Gray Swan benchmark.

concepts.name: Quantum–classical hybrid compute
concepts.desc: Quantum processors scheduled next to GPUs and CPUs in one environment, mainly for real-time error correction.
signals: 12 Nov
Q-CTRL raises US$290M, led by Salesforce Ventures with AMD Ventures joining, to scale AI-driven quantum control software.
12 Nov
AMD plans an equity stake in PsiQuantum and the two tune an ML decoder, PRISM, for real-time error correction on accelerators.
12 Nov
Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN and IBM pass 12,000 atoms in quantum-classical drug binding simulation.
11 Nov
IBM Quantum Platform unifies HPC and quantum in a managed environment.

concepts.name: Cell-state foundation models
concepts.desc: Biology models that predict effects per cell type and state, not per tissue average.
signals: 11 Nov
AlphaGenome 2 released: 107M+ cell profiles, direction-of-effect accuracy 43%.

concepts.name: Humanoids in commercial work
concepts.desc: Robots moving from demos into shops, pharmacies, warehouses and public markets.

OpenAI folds its robotics team into core research, says GPT-6 Astra can control robots directly, and targets a humanoid demo in 2027.

Neura and E.ON plan 4NE1 humanoid trials at substations in 2027; SF Standard questions defence humanoid startup Foundation's contract claims.

SoftBank leads $500M round in Agile Robots at $8.5B; stated capacity 10,000 humanoids a year, shipments undisclosed.

Galbot shows a wheeled, two-armed robot for retail and factory tasks at Web Summit.

Agility begins trading on Nasdaq as AGLT.

eras.name: Large language models
eras.short: Models trained to predict the next word turn out to write, translate and code.
eras.how: A transformer is trained on a large share of the public internet to predict the next token. Capabilities appear with scale: GPT-3 could do tasks it was never trained for, given a few examples in the prompt.
eras.built: Autocomplete, text generation APIs, early GitHub Copilot.
eras.broke: Raw models ramble, make things up and do not follow instructions reliably.

eras.name: Chatbots
eras.short: Instruction tuning and human feedback make models useful in a conversation.
eras.how: Fine-tune the base model on examples of good answers, then use reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) so it prefers helpful, safe replies.
eras.built: Chat interfaces, customer support bots, writing assistants.
eras.broke: The model only knows its training data and cannot look anything up or do anything.

eras.name: RAG and tool use
eras.short: Models get access to your documents and to APIs.
eras.how: Retrieval-augmented generation fetches relevant documents and pastes them into the prompt. Function calling lets the model output a structured call to an API you define.
eras.broke: One question, one answer. Multi-step tasks still needed a human driving every step.

eras.name: Workflows
eras.short: Engineers chain model calls into fixed pipelines.
eras.how: You write the steps in code: classify, then retrieve, then draft, then check. The model fills in each step, but the control flow is yours.
eras.built: Document processing pipelines, LangChain-style chains, eval harnesses.
eras.broke: Fixed pipelines break on anything you did not anticipate. Real tasks need the system to decide what to do next.

eras.name: Agents
eras.short: The model decides the next step itself, in a loop with tools.
eras.how: A loop: the model looks at the goal and results so far, picks a tool, runs it, reads the output, repeats until done. Reasoning models that think before answering made these loops far more reliable.
eras.built: Coding agents, computer-use agents, MCP servers that expose tools to any agent.
eras.broke: Agents worked for minutes, then drifted, looped or lost track on long tasks.

eras.name: Autonomous agents
eras.short: Agents run for hours on real work in sandboxes, with little supervision.
eras.how: Better long-horizon training, sandboxed environments, checkpoints and the ability to run tests let an agent own a whole task: open the repo, make the change, run CI, open a pull request.
eras.built: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity; agents opening PRs while you sleep.
eras.broke: One agent is one thread of work. Large problems need many in parallel.

eras.name: Multi-agent orchestration
eras.short: A planner agent splits work across specialist agents.
eras.how: An orchestrator breaks a goal into subtasks, hands them to worker agents with different tools or prompts, and merges the results.
eras.built: Agent teams for research, code migration and analysis; orchestration frameworks.
eras.broke: Coordination overhead grows fast, and someone still has to check every worker’s output.

eras.name: Agent swarms with verifiers
eras.short: Hundreds to thousands of agents work against an automatic checker that accepts only correct results.
eras.how: Instead of trusting agents, you trust the verifier: a proof checker, test suite or simulator. Agents propose, the verifier filters, survivors get refined. Memory layers start letting agents keep what they learn.
eras.built: 1,000-agent formal proof of Fermat in ~30h; AI-designed quantum circuits beating human designs; Signal's crypto code verified by agents in Lean.
eras.broke: Still open: it only works where a strict automatic check exists.
eras.marks: Fermat formalization (9 Nov 2026), AI quantum circuits (10 Nov 2026), AlphaProof Code on Signal (10 Nov 2026)

eras.name: World models and continual learning
eras.short: Contenders for what comes next: models that learn physics from observation and keep learning after deployment.
eras.how: World models simulate how an environment will change when you act, which lets agents plan in the physical world. Continual learning updates the model from experience without retraining from scratch.
eras.built: Research prototypes, robotics simulation, NeurIPS 2026 workshops.
eras.broke: Not yet reliable outside labs. Watch Frontier for signals.
eras.marks: Genie, V-JEPA, Continual World Models workshop (NeurIPS 2026)
